cur-fossil-ediacara.dateNote: In 1946 the geologist Reg Sprigg found soft-bodied fossils in these South Australian hills. They are about 555 million years old — older than the Cambrian, and among the first large living things. A 2026 study of the rocks at the base of the Ediacara Member in the Flinders Ranges (Faehnrich et al., Earth and Planetary Science Letters, doi 10.1016/j.epsl.2026.120285) found valleys up to about 280 m deep and 6 km wide. The authors argue they began as submarine canyons cut when sea level fell, then were flooded and filled rapidly as it rose again, which may explain why the soft-bodied fossils were so well preserved.

cur-fossil-alcoota.dateNote: In 1962 fossil bones were found on Alcoota Station, north-east of Alice Springs. Digs since have found thousands of bones, among them the giant flightless bird Dromornis stirtoni, one of the biggest birds ever. They are about 8 million years old (Late Miocene).
cur-fossil-alcoota.summary: A bonebed in central Australia with one of the biggest birds that ever lived.
